name: Ashen-Vestment
geological_features: Ash plains hundreds of meters deep
Lava tube caverns with mineral stalactites
specific_features: Ash layers that preserve chemical signatures of billions of years of eruptions
Thermophilic bacteria that form visible colored bands in fumarole runoff
description: Ashen-Vestment is draped in layers of volcanic ash so deep and extensive that the original surface topology is entirely buried. The planet's six active volcanic regions continuously add to this ashen mantle, each eruption depositing a new stratum atop billions of years of accumulated fallout. The ash plains are soft and treacherous, capable of swallowing vehicles that stray from surveyed paths, and the low gravity allows ash particles to remain suspended in the toxic atmosphere for months after major eruptions.

The atmosphere is a gray-brown haze of sulfur compounds and suspended particulates that reduces surface visibility to a few hundred meters on clear days and near zero during eruption events. Fumarole fields punctuate the ash plains with clusters of hissing vents that stain the surrounding terrain in vivid yellows, oranges, and reds as mineral-laden steam condenses on contact with the cooler surface. The planet seems to breathe, a slow exhalation of heat and chemistry that never pauses.

The ash layers function as a geological archive of extraordinary resolution, each stratum preserving the chemical composition of its parent eruption in precise detail. Vulcanologists have mapped eruption histories stretching back four billion years, tracking the evolution of the planet's mantle chemistry through deep time. Thermophilic bacteria thrive in the fumarole runoff, forming brilliantly colored biofilms that are visible against the gray ash backdrop like splashes of paint on a monochrome canvas.

The volcanic ash itself is the planet's most commercially valuable resource, its mineral composition making it an ideal precite for high-performance construction cement used in space station fabrication. Harvesting is straightforward, the material literally covering the planet, but transportation through the particulate-laden atmosphere corrodes standard ship hulls at alarming rates. Specialized vessels with ceramic-coated exteriors service the extraction operations, their crews rotating on short schedules to minimize exposure to the corrosive atmospheric chemistry.
